identity.title: Cirrhosis stigmata: spider angiomata, palmar erythema, gynecomastia, caput medusae, jaundice

technique.how: Inspect face, neck, upper chest, arms and hands in good light for spider angiomata (central arteriole that blanches with pressure and refills centrally), palmar erythema (thenar/hypothenar), gynecomastia, dilated periumbilical veins (caput medusae) and scleral/skin jaundice. Percuss and palpate the liver edge and check for ascites at the same time.
technique.prerequisites: Adequate lighting and skin exposure of the upper body; known or suspected liver disease so the pretest probability is meaningful.

interpretation.positive_finding: Spider nevi (pooled LR 4.3) or clinical ascites (pooled LR 7.2) substantially raise the probability of biopsy-proven cirrhosis in a patient with liver disease.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of individual stigmata does little to exclude cirrhosis; absence of hepatomegaly (LR 0.37) and laboratory indices (platelets >=160, Lok index) are the useful negatives.
interpretation.pitfalls: Isolated spider nevi occur in pregnancy, estrogen use and healthy people; stigmata are late-stage findings and compensated cirrhosis is often stigmata-free. The clinician's overall gestalt was less informative than individual findings.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: treat as probable cirrhosis (screen for varices, SBP, HE; adjust drugs). Negative: do not exclude; use platelets/INR-based indices or elastography.

estimates.target_condition: Cirrhosis (histologically proven) in adults with known or suspected liver disease; finding = spider nevi
estimates.population: 19,533 patients from 86 studies of adults with liver disease undergoing biopsy; prevalence 24%

estimates.target_condition: Cirrhosis (histologically proven) in adults with known or suspected liver disease; finding = ascites on examination
Cirrhosis; finding = absence of hepatomegaly (negative finding)

sources.citation: Udell JA, Wang CS, Tinmouth J, et al. Does this patient with liver disease have cirrhosis? JAMA. 2012;307(8):832-842.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use stigmata to exclude cirrhosis in a patient with risk factors; compensated cirrhosis is frequently silent.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Stigmata plus confusion, GI bleeding, fever with ascites, or rising creatinine indicate decompensation (HE, variceal bleed, SBP, HRS) needing urgent work-up.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: The RCE notes the overall clinician impression was less informative than individual findings; agreement for individual stigmata is not reported in the abstract.

extraction_notes: Only the abstract of the 2012 RCE is accessible (JAMA, not PMC). Pooled LRs for spider nevi, ascites and absent hepatomegaly were taken verbatim from the abstract; the RCE tables reporting palmar erythema, gynecomastia, caput medusae, jaundice and sensitivity/specificity could not be viewed, so those items and sens/spec are left null. Negative LRs for spider nevi/ascites are not in the abstract. Status partially_quantified because only LR+ is available for the stigmata.
